title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
A platform receiving 13 million monthly visitors hosted deepfake pornographic videos featuring Dutch celebrities, politicians, and members of the royal family without authorization. The videos were created by manipulating images and video of real people to depict them in sexual situations. The platform's business model paid users based on view counts, creating financial incentive to produce and upload this content.

This is a failure of content moderation at deployment. The system was not designed to detect and remove nonconsensual sexual imagery before it reached viewers, nor to prevent uploaders from profiting from it. Catching this would have required either automated detection of deepfake pornography before publication or human review of uploads, combined with removal of financial incentive for this class of content.

It is not established whether the platform was aware of the content, knowingly failed to remove it, or was unaware of its presence.

summary:
Multiple Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in fake pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature manipulated content involving Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos appalling and urged victims to file complaints. Managers and representatives confirmed that some victims have already filed reports or are considering legal proceedings.

Deepfake pornography is considered revenge porn and is therefore illegal under Dutch law. Users who upload the material receive payment based on view counts, creating financial incentive to produce more content. Legal experts advise victims to file complaints with authorities, potentially leading to website shutdowns. Additional options include filing group lawsuits, submitting complaints to data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, TV presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued a case resulting in a conditional 180-hour task sentence for a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
